title: Initialization, restart and asynchronous state
prerequisites: These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
Assets validated; SDK controller/adapter created once for the intended lifecycle.
Install asynchronous event/error listeners before sending operations.
sequence: Submit the version-specific Start event once; keep UI operations pending until its result arrives.
Inspect both result type and status; query/consume state before enabling actions.
Route callbacks to the app state machine and dispatch UI updates onto the platform UI thread.
Use the dedicated Restart event when the documented SDK transition requires it; do not repeatedly reconstruct controllers.
On timeout, capture pending operation, last event and error fields rather than replaying a mutation.
expected_result: Cold start reports a valid result/state.
checklist: Cold start reports a valid result/state.
A second tap cannot enqueue duplicate starts.
Restart completion is handled separately from start completion.
Listeners remain attached and obsolete callbacks do not update a replaced screen.
failure_handling: Start success does not mean activation or login succeeded.
Unexpected result type and InvalidState are explicit failures, not successful empty callbacks.

MCSDK 15.16 release notes add automatic foreground/background suspend/resume and SDK-state queries. Match lifecycle handling to the delivered SDK generation; do not add duplicate manual transitions from older examples.

platform_notes.android: StartResultEvent, RestartResultEvent and the state machine are handled asynchronously through the adapter.
platform_notes.ios: KSMStartResultEvent and KSMRestartResultEvent are distinct; the sample checks status before reporting completion.

qualification.note: Examples compile against the exact classic MCSDK/KSSIDP artifact in each example validation record. Compilation and synthetic diagnostics do not qualify a complete live app flow.

android.code:
import com.kobil.wrapper.events.*

fun createRestart(locale: String, version: AppVersion, appName: String,
    mcConfig: String, certificateChain: String, sdkConfig: ByteArray,
    serverBackend: String): RestartEvent =
    RestartEvent(locale, version, appName, mcConfig, certificateChain, sdkConfig)
        .apply { this.serverBackend = serverBackend }

fun stateRequest(): GetSdkStateEvent = GetSdkStateEvent()
fun returnedState(event: EventFrameworkEvent): SdkState? =
    (event as? GetSdkStateResultEvent)?.sdkState
// Route StartResultEvent and RestartResultEvent separately; inspect their
// status/state before enabling actions. A state query is asynchronous too.
